status_summary: No border adjustment of the recommended kind, one denying a deduction for imports and exempting export income, was found in an enacted law, an introduced bill or an administration proposal; the Clean Competition Act (S. 3523 and H.R. 6787), introduced and referred to committee on 2025-12-17, would create a carbon border adjustment based on carbon intensity, a different measure. The Joint Economic Committee scheduled a hearing for 2026-03-04 on a destination-based cash flow tax, a form of border-adjusted tax, after the Supreme Court's tariff ruling; the committee's page lists it as postponed with no new date. The administration's trade agenda has relied on tariffs under executive and trade-statute authority (see c26-01).
title: Consider a border adjustment tax as part of the trade agenda
uncertainties: No border adjustment was found in an enacted law, an introduced bill or an administration proposal that matches the recommendation. The Joint Economic Committee hearing set for 2026-03-04 on a destination-based cash flow tax is listed as postponed, and a member's February 2026 advocacy is not an action. An external retrieval of Congress.gov and web searches (20 queries, run 2026-10-22; it cannot be reproduced here) found no bill that generally denies a deduction for imports and exempts export income. It found related bills, six of which had their status records opened on govinfo.gov: the Clean Competition Act (S. 3523 and H.R. 6787), the Foreign Pollution Fee Act of 2025 (S. 1325), the Methane Border Adjustment Mechanism Act (H.R. 480), the MARKET CHOICE Act (H.R. 3338) and H.R. 6636. Each was referred to committee and shows no later floor or committee action. The titles of the first five describe carbon, pollution, methane or greenhouse gas measures, a different design from a general border adjustment tax; the status records carry no bill text, so this reading rests on titles. H.R. 6636 is titled only To advance sensible priorities, was introduced 2025-12-11 and referred to 21 committees, and its status record carries no text or summary, so its content is unconfirmed. These bills are treated as related context and do not move the stage. The external retrieval also reports no White House, Treasury or Federal Register proposal for a general border adjustment tax. Public Law 119-21 was read only through U.S. Code notes, and the congress.gov search could not be opened here. The only Federal Register border adjustment item concerns the EU carbon measure. The Treasury Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026') lists no such rulemaking; the tax would need legislation, so the agenda is a weak test. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19; external retrieval results and bill status records added 2026-10-22.
